# The Forge — Fractional CFO Action Plan

## INCREASE REVENUE

• **Price increase urgently.** AR/M (revenue per active member) has collapsed from £170.43 (Dec) to £120.48 (June) — that's a 29% slide. You've grown member count to 147 but revenue per head is broken. Audit current pricing tiers; raise standard membership by £5–10/month and trial price for new joiners. Target: restore AR/M to £155+ within 2 months.

• **Churn spike in Q2 (Apr–Jun average 6.7% vs Q1 average 3.4%) is killing retention gains.** The relocation may have disrupted service. Implement a post-relocation reactivation campaign (emails, free trial class offers to lapsed members) and assign one staff member to member onboarding/check-ins. Cap churn at 2%.

• **Upsell class packs & add-ons.** June revenue jumped £2.5k month-on-month but profit fell 55% — non-people expenses soared to £9,390 (likely Class Pass fees, software, venue extras). Bundle personal training sessions or nutrition coaching into membership tiers; charge £3–5/class for drop-ins or multi-packs to convert casual usage into recurring revenue.

• **Fill the quiet hours.** The bigger studio (2x size) means more capacity. Analyse class attendance by time slot. Offer £15/month "off-peak" memberships (7–10am, 2–4pm) and corporate lunch-hour blocks to tap daytime demand without cannibalizing peak pricing.

• **Non-people expenses are out of control.** June: £9,390 (53% of revenue). May: £9,233. Compare to Dec (5,651, 27% of revenue) — you're spending 2x more. # Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your dream list** — Pull your last 3 months of actual transactions. What are members *actually buying*? Build your menu around proven revenue streams first, then add 1-2 new offerings. Grace, you likely have 5-7 core things happening; don't bury them under 20 options.

• **Create two separate, brutally honest menus** — Coach menu shows margins, upsell triggers, and member progression paths (so they know when to pitch small-group training vs. 1:1). Member menu strips out pricing psychology jargon—clear price, clear what's included, one sentence on outcome. Test the member version on 3 non-members; if they don't immediately get it, rewrite.

• **Embed the menu into your sales process today** — Don't wait for the "perfect" design. Screenshot it, send it to every inquiry this week. Track which offerings get questions (signals confusion) and which get purchased (signals demand). Update based on real responses, not assumptions.

• **Coach menu must answer one question per service: "When do I recommend this?"** — Ambiguity kills your team's confidence to sell. Next to each service, write the *exact* member situation that triggers it (e.g., "Recommend group classes for retention; recommend 1:1 for injury/technical gaps").

## Insights

**You've cracked the code in July.** Lead volume jumped 10x (20 to 215), cost-per-lead collapsed from £21 to £2, and you finally converted—29 sales at 14% close rate. This isn't noise; something fundamental shifted. Either your creative, targeting, or offer messaging resonated where it hadn't before, or you hit a genuinely responsive audience segment you weren't reaching in Apr–Jun.

**Apr–Jun was broken.** You were haemorrhaging money on low-intent leads at premium CPL (£6–£21). Zero sales suggests the leads were either wrong-fit (wrong audience), low-intent (wrong message), or the sales process wasn't ready. July's 14% close rate proves the *leads themselves* can convert—so Apr–Jun wasn't just bad timing; it was bad targeting or creative.

**Your unit economics now work, but margin is thin.** At £2 CPL and 14% close, you're generating £29 sales per 100 leads (£58 gross profit per 100 leads = £0.58 per £1 spend). That's viable but tight. You need to either scale what worked in July, improve close rate above 14%, or reduce CPL further—you can't grow profitably if close rate drops back to 0%.

---

## Actions

**1. Audit and lock down July's winning variable immediately.** Pull your July creatives, targeting parameters (age, location, interests, lookalikes, placements), and offer angle. Screenshot or document exactly what ran. Did you change the CTA, add video, shift to Reels, narrow targeting to Belfast postcodes, or adjust the trial offer? Run July's exact setup again in August as your control. If it repeats the 215 leads / £2 CPL / 14% close, you've found your playbook. If it doesn't, something external (seasonal, algorithm, audience saturation) drove July—be ready to pivot.
